serviceHero.headline: Life and Annuity Insurance
serviceHero.subline: Protect the people who depend on you and plan for a steady retirement income. We compare term, whole life, and annuity options from leading carriers to find the right fit for your goals and budget.

whatItCovers.headline: What Life and Annuity Insurance Covers

included.title: Term Life Insurance
included.description: Affordable coverage for a set period — typically 10, 20, or 30 years. Pays a tax-free death benefit to your beneficiaries if you pass away during the term.

included.title: Whole Life Insurance
included.description: Permanent coverage that lasts your entire life, with fixed premiums and a guaranteed cash value that grows over time.

included.title: Universal & Indexed Universal Life
included.description: Permanent coverage with flexible premiums and death benefits. Indexed policies can credit interest based on a market index, with a floor to protect against losses.

included.title: Fixed & Fixed Indexed Annuities
included.description: Grow retirement savings tax-deferred with a guaranteed minimum rate or index-linked growth, while protecting your principal from market downturns.

included.title: Income Annuities
included.description: Turn a lump sum into guaranteed income for a set number of years or for life, so you don't outlive your savings.

excluded.title: Suicide Clause
excluded.description: Most life policies do not pay the death benefit if the insured dies by suicide within the first two years of the policy.

excluded.title: Misrepresentation on the Application
excluded.description: During the contestability period (usually two years), the carrier can deny a claim if health or lifestyle information on the application was inaccurate.

excluded.title: Early Annuity Withdrawals
excluded.description: Withdrawing more than the free amount during the surrender period can trigger surrender charges, and withdrawals before age 59½ may face IRS penalties.

whatItCovers.whoNeedsIt: If anyone depends on your income — a spouse, children, aging parents, or business partners — life insurance makes sure they can cover the mortgage, daily expenses, and education if something happens to you. Annuities are a good fit if you are approaching retirement and want guaranteed income or a safe place to grow savings tax-deferred.

rateFactors.headline: What Affects Your Life Insurance Premium

factors.description: Premiums are lowest when you are young. Every year you wait to buy coverage, the cost increases.
Conditions such as diabetes, heart disease, or high blood pressure affect your underwriting class and price.
Smokers typically pay two to three times more than non-smokers for the same coverage.
Permanent policies cost more than term, and a larger death benefit or longer term raises the premium.
Early heart disease or cancer in parents or siblings can affect your rate class.
Hazardous jobs, private piloting, or high-risk hobbies may add to the premium.

tips: Buy coverage while you are young and healthy to lock in a lower rate
Consider term life for large, temporary needs like a mortgage or raising children
Quitting tobacco for 12 months or more can qualify you for non-smoker rates
Review your policy and beneficiaries after marriage, a new child, or a home purchase

items.question: How much life insurance do I need?
items.answer: A common starting point is 10–15 times your annual income, but the right amount depends on your debts, mortgage, children's education, and other savings. We'll help you calculate a number that fits your family.

items.question: What is the difference between term and whole life insurance?
items.answer: Term life covers you for a set period and is the most affordable option. Whole life lasts your entire life and builds cash value, but costs more. Many families combine the two.

items.question: Do I need a medical exam?
items.answer: Not always. Many carriers offer simplified or accelerated underwriting with no exam for qualifying applicants. Larger coverage amounts or certain health histories may require one.

items.question: What is an annuity and how does it work?
items.answer: An annuity is a contract with an insurance company. You pay a lump sum or a series of payments, and in return the money grows tax-deferred and can later be converted into guaranteed income for a set period or for life.

items.question: Can I access money in an annuity before retirement?
items.answer: Most annuities allow a free withdrawal each year (often up to 10%). Larger withdrawals during the surrender period may incur charges, and withdrawals before age 59½ may face a 10% IRS penalty.
